newsitem.title: QATAR: U.S. firm announces vehicle deal with Kuwaiti guards.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firm announces vehicle deal with Kuwaiti guards.

text.p: AV Technology International (AVT-I), an affiliate of U.S. Lockheed Martin Corp announced on Saturday it would supply Kuwait's National Guard with 70 Pandur 6x6 light armoured vehicles in six variants.

The multi-million dollar deal was unveiled in an AVT-I statement given to reporters at the sidelines of the first International Exhibition of Police and Companies Security Equipment "Milipol 96" which opened in Doha on Saturday.
The deal includes armoured personnel carriers equipped with heavy machineguns and 81 mm mortars as well as an ambulance variant.

AVT-I did not give the value of the contract signed on October 16 "after two years of rigorous filed trials and technical evaluation" but said that with options, it could exceed a delivery of over 200 vehicles.
Industry sources estimated its value at up to $200 million.

The vechicles will be delivered over a period of 24 months along with a comprehensive Integrated Logistics Support programme. AVT-I will also train members of the Kuwaiti National Guard at the Aberdeen Test Centre in Maryland.
David Merry, head of AVT-I's business development weapons systems, told Reuters his firm hoped to reach a similar deal with Qatar.
"I understand Qatar is potentially looking for such vehicles and hopefully we might clinch a deal," he added. "That is why I am here".
About 187 international companies from over 52 countries are displaying their products at the Doha fair.
